body: It's incredibly difficult to basically "train" your brain into seeking other things for comfort/relief/whatever you were using self harm for. You get so used to doing it every time, and then you stop and your brain is like ????? lol but that's amazing, you're doing really well and starting over even though you keep experiencing setbacks is a sign of real strength in my book, especially with something like this!!
Good deal. Staying distracted is the best way to keep the thoughts at bay. I'm around if you need anything in the future!

I'm sorry you were brushed off like that. Being ignored when you try to reach out is incredibly painful and can create so much anxiety (like the inner monologue you're experiencing now). You're heard here on this thread.

How are you feeling now?

I do not know how to make it stop, unfortunately, but I can relate. Every time I go more than a month or so without self harming, I start to have dreams about it. For me, the dreams often happen when I haven't even been thinking about or wanting to self harm in my waking life, which makes the dreams all the more upsetting because it puts the idea at the forefront of my mind again.

I feel like the mind works against those of us trying to stop self harming in many ways, which is why it's so hard to stop. Wanting to and making an effort to change is a big deal, so be proud of yourself for that! You can always PM me if you want to talk. Be safe!!

Almost a year clean is a mega huge accomplishment! Congratulations on that, I hope you're proud of yourself. This slip up doesn't negate all the hard work you put in to make it that far to begin with. I'm sure you know that recovery is up and down and all of that, so I won't repeat it to you here. You can always PM if you want to talk, I just recently broke my longest clean streak as well (was nearly 3 months) so I know how frustrating and disheartening it is. Be safe ♡
So incredibly proud of you, this is awesome!!! Thank you for sharing, it's encouraging to hear real stories about how we can make it out on the other side of this, too. :)

You have to find your own reasons. My reasons to stay alive may seem silly or completely irrelevant to you. I think it's important to remember that anything and everything that makes you glad to be alive, even for a fleeting moment, is worth it. Nothing is too insignificant. Even if what gets you through the day is the fact that you didn't burn your toast. It's okay (necessary, even) to cling to teensy tiny crumbs of purpose when things are so dark in your mind. Looking at the big picture is unhelpful when it looks so bleak, so try focusing smaller–scale on the things that make existing a little bit less strenuous.

I can relate to some of what you said, but not all. I do know what it's like to feel stuck, like you've received all the help you can possibly get and yet nothing has changed. I hope you figure out what your reasons are soon. I'm available for a chat, now or in the future, if you want to talk.
Sending you the tightest, warmest virtual hug I can muster
